title: The three notice decision operations of the D7.1 approval have no REST row in the Ownership Map or in appendix T-A
source: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 (published interface NoticeApi); TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map v1 (P6 REST operations provided, 11 rows); RWB-P7-E2014-CON
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 16 Test cases
description: The legacy story approves, changes and rejects a demand or recall notice through three Java methods of the P6 published interface — NoticeApi.approve(noticeId, decisionLogEntryId), NoticeApi.regenerate(noticeId, templateCode) and NoticeApi.hold(noticeId, reasonCode, decisionLogEntryId) — which P7 calls in process. The TSD P6 endpoint inventory lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 and none of them moves a notice out of state Generated: the notice is created (API-P6-001), read (API-P6-002) and dispatched outside the inventory, and the Ownership Map P6 row repeats the same eleven operations. In the target the in-process call becomes a contract call over the P7 service boundary (DP-11), so the three operations need a path, a request and an answer that no source holds; RWB-P7-E2014-CON consumes them and cannot fix them on its own because the owner is P6.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12: "void approve(UUID noticeId, UUID decisionLogEntryId); NoticeRef regenerate(UUID noticeId, String templateCode); void hold(UUID noticeId, String reasonCode, UUID decisionLogEntryId)"; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 POST /cases/{caseId}/notices to API-P6-011 POST /signature-requests/{requestId}/result with no notice-state operation; Ownership Map v1 P6 REST row lists the same eleven operations.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-014 (section 12 published interface NoticeApi, AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6)
proposed: Publish the three operations on the rwb-comms contract as POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve, .../regenerate and .../hold, with decisionLogEntryId and reasonCode in the request of approve and hold and templateCode in the request of regenerate, the notice as the answer and the 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 set of section 12.1; add the three rows to the rwb-comms API file and to the Ownership Map at the next revision, and keep them in RWB-P7-E2014-CON as consumed operations.

title: The notice table has no column for the decision entry reference that the approve and hold calls carry
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (notice field list); Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 (decisionLogEntryId) and section 11 (DF-DEC-053 decision_log_id on approval)
description: Both the approve and the hold call of the legacy interface take the identifier of the decision log entry, which is how the notice move is tied to the approval that caused it. TSD P6 T3.1 gives the notice table fifteen fields — id, case_id, document_id, notice_type, sent_date, barcode, callback_date, delivery_status, sent_type, party_id, template_id, hold_reason, dispatch_file_id, dispatch_attempts and the standard columns — and not one of them carries that reference; the legacy story instead holds decision_log_id on the approval row of P7 (DF-DEC-053), which is the other side of the same link and lives in another service. Without the column the notice cannot answer which approval moved it, and a held notice cannot show its approver.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12: "POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve ... Response 200 DecisionLogEntry" and "NoticeApi.approve(UUID noticeId, UUID decisionLogEntryId)"; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice rows DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034 with no decision or approval reference; TSD P6 T3.1 has no approval_id or decision_log_entry_id row.
proposed: Add the nullable column decision_log_entry_id uuid to notice in rwb_comms with a unique index, in the Flyway step V2014_1__notice_decision_reference.sql, written by approve and hold and left null on a notice that no approval has moved; add the field to the logical data model for rwb_comms before the wave 2 build.

title: No source says whether a change of template variant replaces the notice row or creates a new version of it
source: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 7, AC2 and section 9; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-ALT-P6-007-01
description: The legacy flow says that on a change the new notice version from the chosen template replaces the proposed one on the approval, and AC2 says that only the changed notice reaches the dispatch run, while AC-ALT-P6-007-01 of the FSD keeps the old document and its template version readable after a new version is made. The notice table holds one document_id and one template_id and has no version-of-a-notice row, no superseded flag and no parent reference, so neither the identity of the notice after the change (same notice ID or a new one) nor the fate of the superseded document is fixed. The approval refers to the notice by source_ref, which makes the answer material to RWB-P7-E2014-APP.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 7: "the new notice version replaces the proposed one on the approval"; AC2: "the system generates a new notice version from DEMAND-MTG-B and is the one approved"; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice rows DF-LEG-017 document_id and DF-LEG-031 template_id, single-valued, with no version chain column.
proposed: Regenerate on the same notice row: document_id and template_id move to the chosen Approved variant, the standard version column increments, and the previous document stays in rwb-document with its template version as AC-ALT-P6-007-01 requires, so the approval keeps one source_ref for the life of the notice; state the rule in the rwb-comms API file so RWB-P7-E2014-APP and the ITG evidence read the same identity.

title: The notice answer has no field list, and the template state the approval panel must show is not part of it
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.2 (API-P6-002 Response Notice) and T3.1; Legacy RWB-E2-014 AC6, AC10 and section 12; RWB-P7-E2014-CON
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.1; 12.8; 15 Screens and states
description: The read of a notice answers a resource the appendix calls Notice, with no property list in any row. The legacy AC6 turns on the panel knowing that the template version which produced the notice has been withdrawn, and AC10 shows the template code and version on the screen, so the answer must carry the template code, the template version and the state of that version; the notice row holds only template_id, and the code, version, product group and state are columns of template. Whether the answer flattens those three template facts, how the document reference is expressed, and which fields the route may show without a second call are therefore fixed by the P7 screen contract and not by any source of P6.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 API-P6-002: "Response Notice", errors 401, 403, 404, 503, no property list; TSD P6 T3.1 notice row holds DF-LEG-031 template_id only; Legacy RWB-E2-014 AC6: "Then the screen shows MSG-P6-003" and AC10: "template DEMAND-MTG version 2".
proposed: Baseline the notice answer in RWB-P7-E2014-CON and the rwb-comms API file as id, caseId, documentId, noticeType, state, templateCode, templateVersion, templateState, approvedAt and decisionLogEntryId, mapped from notice and template in rwb_comms with no personal field, and declare it as the summary the route composes; the template state values are DRAFT, APPROVED and WITHDRAWN as TSD P6 T-A.2 uses them.

title: The declared right of the three notice decision operations is not in the endpoint inventory or the RBAC matrix
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2; appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 10
description: TSD P6 T6.2 states that each endpoint declares its capability area and right, and the matrix of T6.1 gives RW-LITOFF Litigation CRUA and RW-LEGAL Litigation RA, while appendix T-A.2 declares the area and right of the eleven endpoints it lists. The three operations that move a notice out of Generated are in neither list, so no source says whether they are declared as Litigation right A of the approver (the legacy authority table gives the approver Litigation A for D7.1), whether they require a service identity because the caller is rwb-decision and not the browser, or how the approver's identity reaches rwb-comms for the record. DP-08 and the rwb-access contract are not in this key's pattern set, so the local check has no dependency to lean on either.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.2: "each endpoint declares its capability area and right; scope filters every query"; T6.1 rows RW-LITOFF "CRU | CRUA" and RW-LEGAL "CRUA | RA" for Documents and Litigation; T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 only; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 10: "RW-LITOFF ... Approves, changes or rejects D7.1 notices they did not prepare (Litigation A)".
proposed: Declare the three operations as Litigation right A with scope applied, enforced at gateway-bff through the rwb-access contract as the other routes are, and have rwb-decision call them with its service identity plus the approver's user identifier and the decision entry reference in the request, so the record carries the approver; add the three rows to T-A.1 with that right before the wave 2 build.

title: The plan records no build row for the platform contracts that the patterns of this slice add
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-19) and R5.7; plan split slice RWB-P6-E2014-APP (H empty, C = RWB-P7-E2014-CON)
section: Metadata Depends on (build); 3 Preconditions; 13 Solution plan
description: The pattern table adds a platform contract for six of the ten patterns of this story — RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON for the parameters and reference data, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for the outbox and inbox, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON for the workflow kit and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route — together with the two rwb-case contract rows of DP-06 and DP-07. The slice of this story carries an empty H list and a single C row, so the story cannot name those contracts as build dependencies and must reach them through the notice contract baseline of the same service and the published libraries.
evidence: Plan split slice RWB-P6-E2014-APP: "H": [], "C": ["RWB-P7-E2014-CON"], "ready": "Day 1"; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03 "H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON", DP-06 "H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON", DP-07 "H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON", DP-09 "H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON", DP-10 "H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON", DP-19 "H RWB-PLT-N001-CON".
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-014 (section 12 events, section 13 components, section 15 screens)
proposed: Keep the H row empty as the plan fixes it, since every platform contract named is already a dependency of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and of the libraries this service consumes, and add the six platform contracts and the two rwb-case contracts to the C list of the slice at the next plan revision so the story names the contracts it builds against; until then the fakes of 12.8 stand in for them.

title: No source says whether a notice move writes its own decision record or only references the approval entry of rwb-decision
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T2 (published interface) and T4; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 (decisionLogEntryId) and FSD P6 A2.1 step 3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and ADR-022
section: 4 Flow step 8; 8 Business rules BR12; 11 Data; 12.3; 12.7
description: The TSD says the module acts on events from P3 and writes through the decision log of P7, and the legacy contract passes the identifier of the entry that P7 already wrote, which reads as a reference and not as a second record. In the target the decision-record library writes a local record in the writer's own schema and relays it on the shared topic, so a notice move either writes its own record with the approval entry as its reference, or writes nothing and relies on the entry of the approval. The difference decides whether the notice row, the outbox row and the record of the move commit together, which is what makes the fail-closed rule of BR7 provable.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T4: "No case state machine of its own; the module acts on events from P3 and writes through the decision log"; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12: "void approve(UUID noticeId, UUID decisionLogEntryId)"; FSD P6 v3 A2.1.2 step 3: "Writes the decision log entry".
proposed: Let the notice move write one local decision record through the library with decision code D7.1, the rule in force, the notice and case IDs, the template code and version, the state from and to, the reason code where one applies, the approver and the approval entry reference, and let the shared topic carry it; the approval entry of rwb-decision stays the entry of the approval, and the central ledger holds both, which ADR-022 allows.

title: The hold reason vocabulary has no list of values, and the owner namespace of the feature switch is not settled for the comms half
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 hold_reason (TEXT, no list) and T3.2; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 13 (rwb.decision.notice-approval) and section 4 step 9; FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-EXC-P6-001-02
description: hold_reason is typed varchar(30) with the list column empty, so REFUSED_BY_APPROVER and TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN are used by the legacy story and by the FSD exception flow but held nowhere as reference data, and no source fixes whether the value set is a LOV of rwb-case or a value set of this service. In the same way the legacy feature flag is named rwb.decision.notice-approval on the decision module, while the operations that the flag closes belong to rwb-comms; no source says whether the key keeps that name, and whether the two services read one switch or one each.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-LEG-032 hold_reason TEXT varchar(30) No | None" with the List column empty; TSD P6 T3.2 lists LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-LANG, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-SENT-TYPE, LOV-SIGN-METHOD, LOV-SIGN-STATUS and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS and no hold reason list; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 13: "Feature flag: rwb.decision.notice-approval".
proposed: Add LOV-HOLD-REASON to the reference data of rwb-case with at least REFUSED_BY_APPROVER and TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, or publish the same two values as the value set of the rwb-comms contract, and keep the legacy switch key rwb.decision.notice-approval read by both services until the platform feature-flag owner renames it.
